rfi.title: Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike
rfi.description: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.

rfi.title: Millions of Americans go to the polls in US midterm elections
rfi.description: Millions of Americans will head to the polls on Tuesday for the country's mid-term elections, in a vote that will determine whether the ruling Republicans or opposition Democrats control Congress.

rfi.title: In Miami’s Little Haiti, ‘Blood’ looks past Trump’s rhetoric as US midterms loom
rfi.description: In Miami’s Little Haiti, a man mourning his mother and struggling to find steady work sees opportunity in Donald Trump’s politics. The president’s false claims about Haitian immigrants have not shaken his support. For the man known as Blood, what matters jus before the midterm elections is the promise of a chance to earn a living.

rfi.title: UN confirms start of process to wind up Western Sahara mission
rfi.description: The United Nations confirmed it had begun the process to end its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara after Russia and the United States vetoed each other's draft resolutions on extending the 35-year-old deployment.

rfi.title: Nine out of 10 crimes against journalists go unpunished, Unesco says
rfi.description: Monday marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists – chosen in memory of Ghislaine Dupont and Claude Verlon, two journalists from Radio France Internationale who were murdered in Mali on 2 November, 2013. According to a report by Unesco, attacks and harassment targeting the press continue to go largely unpunished in Africa and across the globe.

rfi.title: Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing
rfi.description: A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man.

rfi.title: Nigerian health chiefs confirm negative results in Ebola cases
rfi.description: Health authorities investigating two suspected Ebola cases in north-eastern Nigeria ​confirmed on Monday that both samples were negative after ‌two rounds of testing.

rfi.title: France braces for fresh protests as students to resume school blockades
rfi.description: France is readying for another week of protests after the head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart Monday, ahead of a nationwide day of strikes and protests on Thursday.

rfi.title: Miami voters weigh local hardship and America's global role as early voting ends
rfi.description: A massive thunderstorm and flash flood warnings failed to deter voters in Miami as they headed to polling stations on Florida’s final day of early voting ahead of the US midterm elections.

rfi.title: A year after the fall of El Fasher, Sudan's war has left a ghost town in its wake
rfi.description: A year after paramilitary forces at war with the Sudanese army captured the strategic city of El Fasher, survivors and aid workers report that the capital of North Darfur state remains largely abandoned. Some residents are too scared to return, while thousands are still missing – many held in deplorable conditions in overcrowded prisons.

rfi.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police
rfi.description: France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.

rfi.title: 'Working in Russia is like being a deep-sea diver', BBC's man in Moscow tells RFI
rfi.description: How does one report, from its capital, on the reality of Russia at war? Based in Moscow for more than 30 years, the BBC's Russia correspondent Steve Rosenberg is one of the few Western journalists still working in the country. He spoke to RFI about his daily life as a reporter in Russia and why he has chosen to stay, despite the Kremlin's increasing hostility to foreign media.

rfi.title: Five British anti-immigration activists arrested in northern France
rfi.description: French police say they've arrested five British far-right activists found carrying tear gas bombs, as they were filming themselves harassing migrants near the northern Channel port of Dunkirk.

rfi.title: Florida Keys business owners reveal contrasting views of Trump's America
rfi.description: Two restaurant owners in the Florida Keys have differing views of Donald Trump's America on the eve of US midterm elections, with a French immigrant concerned about growing political divisions and a Cuban-American restaurateur still sympathetic to Republicans despite misgivings about the president.

rfi.title: 'Protecting the Congo's forests means protecting people's lives'
rfi.description: The forests of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are a haven for some of the world's rarest species – but despite being protected areas, they are under threat from conflict, poaching and deforestation. After global decision-makers gathered at the United Nations' Cop17 biodiversity summit this week, Emmanuel Bahati Lukoo, a ranger at Kahuzi-Biega National Park, says people on the frontline of wildlife protection deserve greater recognition.

rfi.title: Youth Olympics kick off in Senegal with 'magical' opening ceremony
rfi.description: The Youth Olympic Games opened with a spectacular ceremony in Senegal on Saturday, marking the first Olympic event in Africa as the continent seeks a bigger role in international sports competitions.

rfi.title: Why war makes Ukraine media more determined than ever to hold power to account
rfi.description: For Ukrainian media, exposing corruption in times of war is a high-stakes move – with domestic scandals potentially tarnishing the country's image in the eyes of the international partners it relies on. But journalists remain dedicated to their role as a counterbalance to the authorities, believing that upholding democracy is more important now than ever.

rfi.title: 'African leaders are not naive, they will partner with whoever makes the best offer’
rfi.description: The third Russia-Africa Summit took place in Moscow this week, with 48 African nations sending delegations. It comes as Moscow grapples with sanctions and isolation over its Ukraine offensive, while African governments turn to it for security assistance. However, geopolitical analyst Priyal Singh tells RFI that despite this, Russia still lags behind China in its influence on the continent.

euronews.title: The Senate on a razor’s edge: The races that will decide America's midterms
euronews.description: Democrats look all but certain to take the US House. The real fight is for the Senate, where a handful of races in states Republicans never expected to defend will decide who controls Washington.

euronews.title: Hoax bomb threats target four European flights as scares spread across the continent
euronews.description: One of Warsaw’s airports was shut and a Ryanair jet landed in Spain under an emergency protocol, the third straight day that threats have disrupted passenger planes in Europe.

euronews.title: Italy-Albania migration deal could be extended beyond 2028, Rama says
euronews.description: The Albanian prime minister said the migration deal with Italy could be extended at Rome’s request, dispelling doubts about the closure of the centres when the current partnership expires.

euronews.title: Americans head to the polls for US midterm elections
euronews.description: Voters cast their ballots in Fairfax, Virginia, and New York as Americans head to the polls in midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term.

euronews.title: The Zangezur Corridor: Regional peace and global connectivity
euronews.description: The Zangezur Corridor is a test case for the region, writes Dr Matin Mammadli of the Centre for the Analysis of International Relations in Baku in an article for Euronews. It could link Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan, strengthen trade between Europe and Asia, and lay an economic foundation for peace.

euronews.title: A licence to create: Inspired carpets and religious brushstrokes shine at Baku Art Weekend
euronews.description: Transforming a carpet into contemporary art and replacing a painter’s brush with a syringe. Just a few insights into how an art weekend offered new methods of artistic licence to creatives gathering in Baku.

euronews.title: South Korea and Turkey sign financing pact as Seoul seeks role in planned nuclear power plant
euronews.description: Turkey and South Korea are expanding nuclear, defence and trade ties. Their latest agreement explores funding for nuclear projects, while Ankara weighs potential partners for its planned Sinop plant.

euronews.title: UK likely to face AI-powered cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028, cyber chief warns
euronews.description: Criminals and hostile states are increasingly using artificial intelligence to scale up cyber operations, with outdated technology leaving essential services exposed, the head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre says.

euronews.title: Moldova suspects state actor behind major cyberattack, PM tells Euronews
euronews.description: Moldova Prime Minister Vasile told Euronews that a foreign state is suspected of hacking government databases and extracting citizens’ personal identification data. He said the list of suspects was "not very long". The attacks come amid wider cyber incidents across Europe.

euronews.title: Flash floods devastate US Southwest, sweeping away homes and cars
euronews.description: Flash floods sweep across the United States Southwest, destroying homes, stranding residents and forcing hundreds to evacuate.

euronews.title: Costa: Europe's experience demonstrates that enlargement benefits us all
euronews.description: António Costa used his address to the Euronews EU Enlargement Summit to set out why enlargement is an investment rather than a burden, from the 26 million jobs created since 2004 to Montenegro’s push to join by 2028.

euronews.title: Armenia to apply for EU membership in 2027 or 2028 ‘realistic’, PM tells Euronews
euronews.description: Armenia could formally apply to join the EU in 2027 or 2028, PM Nikol Pashinyan told Euronews. He called EU membership a strategic choice to protect democracy, said Armenians must choose between Brussels and Russia’s Eurasian bloc, and rejected warnings that Armenia could become the next Ukraine.

euronews.title: Taylor Red singer Nicole Taylor dies aged 35 after battle with breast cancer
euronews.description: The death of Taylor Red's singer Nicole Taylor was announced by her siblings on YouTube. They described their sister as their "fearless leader".

euronews.title: Earth Now | What does it take to tackle air pollution?
euronews.description: From emissions at busy ports to pollution from industry, traffic, heating and dust, improving air quality means tackling a complex mix of sources. In Turkey and Uzbekistan, different approaches are being taken to reduce emissions and better understand the air people breathe.

euronews.title: Serbia's new leaders unlikely to recognise Kosovo, Albania's Rama warns
euronews.description: Edi Rama says Serbia’s new government remains “completely closed towards recognising Kosovo” and remains reluctant to impose sanctions on Russia.

euronews.title: Philippe Jaenada wins 2026 Prix Goncourt for novel 'L'Inconnue du quai de Javel'
euronews.description: The jury for the Goncourt Prize, France's most prestigious literary award, has delivered its verdict, amid controversy over the dominant role of the Madrigall group in the selections.

euronews.title: Hungary appoints Péter Fejes as new top prosecutor to head anti-graft drive after Orbán downfall
euronews.description: Public confidence in prosecutors eroded under Orbán's 16-year rule, as critics accused the highly centralised institution of shielding the premier's inner circle from scrutiny.

euronews.title: Qatar sees 'hope' for US-Iran deal despite fresh US strikes as mediators exchange proposals in real time
euronews.description: Qatar said Tuesday it saw hope for an interim deal as mediators continue to exchange proposals, despite fresh US strikes and threats to shipping through Hormuz continue to complicate efforts to end the Iran war.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, midterms 2026 : suivez la journée de vote aux Etats-Unis pour les élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis, les dernières informations et les réponses à vos questions
lemonde.description: Plus de 58 millions d’Américains ont déjà voté par anticipation et les bureaux de vote sont ouverts dans tout le pays. Il s’agit d’un record pour des élections de mi-mandat, qui pourraient cette fois-ci voir les démocrates prendre le contrôle de la Chambre des représentants, voire du Sénat, et compromettre la fin du mandat de Donald Trump.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, audition de Laurent Nuñez : les services de renseignement avaient alerté sur « l’ensemble des risques qui se sont avérés exacts le 17 octobre », assure le ministre de l’intérieur devant la commission d’enquête
lemonde.description: La commission doit se pencher, entre autres, sur « la façon dont les pouvoirs publics se préparent en amont de tels événements », mais aussi sur les « renseignements et les moyens dont ils disposent », alors que l’exécutif a reconnu des défaillances et que le ministre de l’intérieur avait remis sa démission − refusée − à Emmanuel Macron.

lemonde.title: Livret A : le plafond sera relevé à « entre 25 000 et 30 000 euros », en février prochain, annonce Sébastien Lecornu
lemonde.description: Le ministre de l’économie, Roland Lescure, précisera le nouveau plafond « dans les semaines qui viendront » à l’issue d’une « dernière concertation » avec les banques et la Caisse des dépôts. Le Livret A est actuellement plafonné à 22 950 euros.

lemonde.title: Le Royaume-Uni durcit sa politique contre l’immigration légale
lemonde.description: Les étrangers en situation régulière seront obligés, dans la plupart des cas, de patienter dix ans avant de pouvoir accéder au statut de résident permanent. Les hauts revenus bénéficieront d’un délai plus court, quand les demandeurs d’asile arrivés sur les « small boats » devront avoir passé au moins vingt ans outre-Manche.

lemonde.title: Comment l’essor des médicaments anti-obésité modifie les habitudes alimentaires
lemonde.description: Moins de produits de boulangerie, de confiseries, de biscuits, de snacks salés, de boissons gazeuses et de sodas : une étude du cabinet Bain, publiée mardi, portant sur des milliers de patients, note une évolution de leur mode de consommation.

lemonde.title: Maylis Adhémar, une enfance sous extrême influence
lemonde.description: Dans « Comment j’ai cessé d’être une petite fasciste », l’écrivaine revient sur sa jeunesse au sein d’une famille intégriste et réactionnaire. Un récit d’émancipation qui sonne comme une charge contre la banalisation de l’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: En Alsace, la hausse des factures de fioul domestique « fait mal » aux ménages
lemonde.description: Dans le pays, près de 9 % des résidences principales sont toujours chauffées au fioul, dont le prix a flambé en un an. Dans le sillage d’une tournée de livraison des maisons du Bas-Rhin, les clients confient leurs appréhensions.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump annonce la fin d’une aide pour la sécurité d’Israël, d’un montant annuel de 3,8 milliards de dollars
lemonde.description: Cette assistance américaine à la sécurité d’Israël avait commencé en 2019, pour une durée de dix ans. L’accord avait été signé trois ans auparavant par Barack Obama.

lemonde.title: Etre une femme politique et devenir mère, le piège de l’injonction contradictoire
lemonde.description: De Ségolène Royal à Marine Tondelier, concilier maternité et fonction politique continue de bousculer un temps politique taillé par et pour les hommes.

lemonde.title: Agression dans une école à Nice : l’autrice était en situation irrégulière et assignée à résidence, annonce Laurent Nuñez
lemonde.description: Interrogé sur cette affaire dans le cadre des questions au gouvernement dans l’Hémicycle, mardi, le ministre de l’intérieur a également dénoncé une agression « insoutenable, intolérable dans une école de la République ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le bilan des frappes russes ciblant une école de Komychouvakha passe à 33 morts
lemonde.description: Les bombardements ont eu lieu dans cette ville de la région de Zaporijia, alors que des distributions d’aide humanitaire s’y déroulaient lundi. Plus de 50 personnes pourraient toujours se trouver sous les décombres, a annoncé mardi le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, lors de sa visite à Berlin.

lemonde.title: La journaliste Vanessa Dougnac, grande spécialiste de l’Inde, est morte à 54 ans
lemonde.description: Elle avait passé vingt-cinq ans de sa vie en Inde, avant d’en être bannie par le gouvernement du nationaliste hindou Narendra Modi en février 2024. Elle a succombé à un cancer le 2 novembre.

lemonde.title: La démocratie de l’eau suit un chemin semé d’embûches
lemonde.description: Le nouveau schéma d’aménagement de l’eau adopté dans le bassin de la Vilaine a été obtenu après de très longues concertations. Ce cas d’école démontre que les compromis environnementaux, produits par des acteurs locaux sous la pression de l’Etat, sont possibles mais demeurent fragiles.

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, les peuples autochtones dénoncent une vague de violences en représailles à la réélection de Lula
lemonde.description: La plupart des cas de violence concernent le peuple Guarani-kaiowa, qui revendique la démarcation de ses terres ancestrales, occupées par des producteurs de soja dans le Mato Grosso do Sul, dans le sud-ouest du pays.

lemonde.title: La bataille pour le climat est-elle féministe ?
lemonde.description: Le changement climatique exacerbe les inégalités de genre et il faut en tenir compte pour réussir la transition. La climatologue Valérie Masson-Delmotte témoigne également de son parcours de chercheuse spécialiste du climat dans un monde masculin.

lemonde.title: Le prix Goncourt est décerné à Philippe Jaenada pour « L’Inconnue du quai de Javel »
lemonde.description: L’écrivain, âgé de 62 ans, est récompensé pour son treizième roman, une enquête sur le meurtre d’une jeune femme, Louise Cansot, en 1949.

zeit.description: Unter anderem Boris Pistorius hat Dobrindt für seine Aussage zu den Ausschreitungen am Wochenende kritisiert. Der Bundesinnenminister bleibt dennoch bei seiner Wortwahl.

zeit.title: Konsequenz aus Vorwürfen: Nach Vorwürfen: Comedy-Veranstaltung mit Palmer abgesagt
52-Millionen-Euro-Investition: Neue Silikonanlage soll Evonik-Standort Essen stärken
Champions League: RB Leipzig mit «Mut und Sauberkeit» gegen Man City
Sporthalle in Oberhausen: Böllerwurf in Umkleidekabine: Zehn Schüler verletzt
Flüge umgeleitet: Mehrere Bombenwarnungen im europäischen Flugverkehr
Oberbürgermeister in Kritik: Belästigungsvorwürfe: Palmer lässt Ehrenamt fürs Land ruhen
Israel: Donald Trump kündigt Ende von Milliardenhilfen für Israel an
zeit.description: US-Finanzhilfen für Israel in Milliardenhöhe sollen zum Jahresende auslaufen. Präsident Donald Trump sagte, die USA würden dem Land stattdessen Waffen verkaufen.

zeit.title: Gipfeltreffen in der Karibik: Keine Entschuldigung von König Charles für Sklaverei
Grenze zu Kaliningrad: Polen reagiert mit Großeinsatz auf »Provokation« an russischer Grenze
zeit.description: An der russisch-polnischen Grenze tauchen nachts Personen auf, der Geheimdienst warnt vor dem Eindringen Bewaffneter. Polen reagiert mit einem Großeinsatz.

zeit.title: Milliardärssteuer: Umfrage sieht Mehrheit gegen Milliardärssteuer in Kalifornien
zeit.description: Es wäre die erste Milliardärssteuer der Welt. Die Volksabstimmung heute in Kalifornien gilt als Test für Reichensteuern weltweit. Laut Umfragen sind die Wähler dagegen.

zeit.title: Midterms in den USA: Können uns die Midterms nicht egal sein?
zeit.description: Für die nächste Präsidentschaftswahl sind die Zwischenwahlen statistisch nicht signifikant. Aber andere Zahlen zeigen: Es geht heute um viel.

zeit.title: Spionageangriff: Wer von den Angriffen auf Politiker-Handys betroffen ist
zeit.description: Apple hat mehrere deutsche Parlamentarier vor einem Spionageangriff auf ihre Mobiltelefone gewarnt. Mindestens sieben Abgeordnete sind darunter – auch eine Parteichefin.

nzz.title: Die Stadt Zürich verliert an bester Lage 127 Parkplätze mit Seesicht
nzz.description: Bald beginnen die Arbeiten an der neuen Promenade beim Hafen Enge.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Midterms 2026: Wahllokale in fast allen US-Gliedstaaten geöffnet +++ Zu dickes Stimmzettelpapier sorgt für Probleme
nzz.description: Am 3. November wählen die Amerikaner einen neuen Kongress. Bei den Midterms entscheidet sich, ob die Republikaner ihre Mehrheiten im Senat und im Repräsentantenhaus halten können. Alle Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Der britische Premierminister wagt bei der Frage nach Reparationszahlungen für die Sklaverei eine Flucht nach vorn
nzz.description: Am jährlichen Treffen der Commonwealth-Staaten spricht der britische König sein tiefes Bedauern über den Sklavenhandel aus. Es ist aber Andy Burnham, der zum ersten Mal in der britischen Geschichte eine offizielle Entschuldigung ankündigt.

nzz.title: «Die kleine Märtyrerin von der A 10»: Fast vierzig Jahre nach dem Fund einer Kindsleiche stehen in Frankreich die Eltern vor Gericht
nzz.description: Jahrzehntelang wusste niemand, wer das tote Mädchen war, das an einer Autobahn abgelegt worden war. Erst eine DNA-Spur führte zur Familie von Inass Touloub. Sie wurde nur vier Jahre alt und musste Schreckliches erleiden.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Signa-Insolvenz: René Benko steht erneut vor Gericht – im Fokus stehen ein teures Jagdgewehr und der Bauunternehmer Hans Peter Haselsteiner
nzz.description: Das Immobilien- und Detailhandelsreich des österreichischen Investors René Benko ist zusammengebrochen. Die Signa-Holding und mehrere Tochtergesellschaften stecken in einem Insolvenzverfahren. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Tausend Parkplätze beim Zoo ersatzlos streichen, dafür eine Tramlinie bis zum Eingang – der VCS zerpflückt die Pläne von Stadt und Kanton
nzz.description: Stadt und Kanton planen für den Zoo ein Parkhaus mit bis zu 1200 Plätzen. Das geht dem grünen Verkehrsclub der Schweiz viel zu weit.

nzz.title: Um die Sicherheit der Schweiz zu stärken: Bundesrat soll Gruppen wie Hamas und Hizbullah schneller verbieten können
nzz.description: Will die Schweiz eine Terrororganisation verbieten, muss sie jeweils ein Spezialgesetz erlassen. Doch präzise Kriterien fehlen, zudem ist dieser Weg langwierig. Nun zeichnet sich ein Systemwechsel ab.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump bestätigt neue Angriffe auf iranische Ziele
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: VIDEO - 50 Grad im Tiefkühler: Wie Hacker Supermärkte sabotieren
nzz.description: In mehreren europäischen Ländern haben Hacker Kühlanlagen von Supermärkten manipuliert. Lebensmittel mussten entsorgt werden. Doch wie können Angreifer die Kühlung aus der Ferne sabotieren? Und kann man sich dagegen schützen?

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - «Gesund ist, was dir guttut»: Die Wohlfühl-Rhetorik der Krankenkassen verabschiedet sich vom Ideal des mündigen Patienten
nzz.description: Die Versicherer umwerben ihre Kunden mit infantilen Slogans. Dabei erfordert Gesundheit nicht Bauchgefühle, sondern die aktive Auseinandersetzung mit der wissenschaftlichen Beweislage.

nzz.title: Wiederholungen und Schwarz-Weiss-Bilder: Tschechiens öffentlichrechtliche Medien protestieren gegen die Abschaffung der Gebühren
nzz.description: Die Regierung von Andrej Babis will die Rundfunkabgaben streichen und die öffentlichrechtlichen Medien stattdessen aus dem Budget finanzieren. Die Opposition befürchtet Staatspropaganda wie in benachbarten Ländern.

nzz.title: Die Alternative Linke in Zürich verlangt ultimativ, dass «rassifizierte Büsten» abgedeckt werden – andernfalls gebe es kein Geld für den Schulhaus-Umbau
nzz.description: Der Anblick sei unzumutbar für Lehrpersonen und Schüler, findet die Partei. Damit entbrennt der Streit um das sogenannte koloniale Erbe neu.

nzz.title: Nach der Waffenruhe ein Massaker: Russischer Angriff auf Schulhaus tötet Dutzende von Zivilisten
nzz.description: Die erfolgreiche Hilfsaktion in Oleschki steht nicht für ein humanitäres Umdenken im Kreml. Russland attackiert die Ukraine weiterhin ohne jegliche Rücksicht auf zivile Opfer. Exemplarisch dafür steht ein besonders blutiger Angriff in der Provinz Saporischja.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Melania Trump kündigt Treffen mit Ukrainern und Russen an
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Hacker lassen Tiefkühltruhen in europäischen Supermärkten auftauen – laut Experten könnte das erst der Anfang sein
nzz.description: Dutzende Lebensmittelfilialen in Nord- und Mitteleuropa sind Opfer von Cyberangriffen geworden. Was in der Tiefkühlabteilung begann, könnte sich in vielen Privathaushalten wiederholen.

nzz.title: Fussball: Lausanne-Sport trennt sich von Trainer Elsner
nzz.description: Nach nur einem Sieg in zwölf Meisterschaftsspielen teilt der Waadtländer Klub die Trennung mit.

observador.title: 16h. Incêndio chegou a Penalva do Castelo e Aguiar da Beira
observador.description: O primeiro alerta foi dado perto das 23h no concelho de Fornos de Algodres, e já tem uma extensão de 10 kms. Anda, pelo menos sete aviões foram alvo de ameaças de bomba nas últimas 24 horas

observador.title: "As exigências do Irão são inaceitáveis para os EUA"
observador.description: O Coronel Carlos Mendes Dias considera que as exigências iranianas para a paz são inaceitáveis tanto para democratas como para republicanos, travando o avanço das negociações.

observador.title: Cuidar dos pais ou ter filhos?
observador.description: Um terço dos jovens portugueses admite que ter de cuidar de um familiar poderia levá-los a adiar a decisão de ter filhos. Primeiro os pais, depois os filhos: ou nunca chega a vez dos filhos?

observador.title: SLB deixou a máquina na garagem, mas ganha 3 pontos na mesma
observador.description: A exibição do SLB frente ao Alverca foi tudo menos vistosa, valeu o penálti salvador para segurar a vitória. À espera do novo técnico, o SCP defronta o Shakhtar a precisar de pontos na Champions.

observador.title: 30 plantas sem encher o caixote do lixo?
observador.description: As famílias portuguesas são das que mais comida deitam fora na Europa, sobretudo fruta e legumes. Conservas e congelados ajudam a variar sem estragar. A Nutricionista Mariana Chaves mostra como.

observador.title: Lidl e WWF unem-se para restaurar a Mata Nacional do Valado
observador.description: Com a venda do saco solidário, o Lidl Portugal entrega 100 mil euros ao restauro da Mata do Valado. Em parceria com a WWF, o objetivo é promover a biodiversidade e prevenir novas catástrofes.

observador.title: Direito de resposta do Maus Hábitos
observador.description: O Observador publica o direito de resposta do Maus Hábitos sobre o artigo "Maus Hábitos: proprietário do prédio diz que não renovou contrato por conflitos' e 'recorrentes incumprimentos e mentiras'".

observador.title: Como vai funcionar o novo apoio à compra de carros elétricos
observador.description: O Governo anunciou um novo apoio à compra de carros elétricos por famílias vulneráveis. O concurso deve ser lançado no início de 2027 e há 1,5 milhões de famílias elegíveis. O que já se sabe?

observador.title: 15h. Caso Cambra. MP quer recurso com efeitos suspensivos
observador.description: MP interpôs recurso para o TC da decisão do Tribunal Administrativo de Lisboa, que autorizou Renata Cambra a acampar no Rossio. Ainda, Incêndio já alastrou a Penalva do Castelo e Aguiar da Beira.

observador.title: 28 mil famílias vão mesmo receber Vale Eficiência
observador.description: Processo simplificado vai permitir que cerca de 28 mil famílias que tinham sido consideradas elegíveis, mas tinham ficado de fora, possam, afinal, receber um vale para combater pobreza energética.

observador.title: Livre quer dialogo sério com o Governo sobre habitação
observador.description: Ministro das Infraestruturas e Habitação abriu a porta a discutir propostas para a habitação com o Livre e mostrou-se disponível para o fazer "com humildade". O Livre quer uma base comum estável.

observador.title: Oposição aceita formar Governo nas condições de Eisenkot
observador.description: Partidos da oposição reafirmaram, durante o encontro, a intenção de propor Eisenkot como candidato à formação de Governo ao Presidente Isaac Herzog, que começa quarta-feira as consultas aos partidos.

observador.title: Fotógrafo Bruno Pereira Ribeiro vence Prémio Narrativa
observador.description: Bruno Pereira Ribeiro venceu o Prémio Narrativa, com "Westernmost", e os projetos "Secret Garden", de Tatiana Iartseva, e "Parque", de David Henriques, receberam menções honrosas.

observador.title: Ataque. Cidadãos pela Cibersegurança pedem esclarecimentos
observador.description: Iniciativa Cidadãos pela Cibersegurança defende que "não está em causa a vida privada de um governante, mas a segurança das comunicações do Estado", exigindo um esclarecimento ao Governo.

observador.title: Bruxelas remete para Lisboa manutenção da ordem pública
observador.description: "É uma questão da competência das autoridades nacionais", afirmou o porta-voz do executivo comunitário para os Assuntos Internos, Democracia, Justiça e Estado de direito, Markus Lammert.

observador.title: IA deverá afetar 40% do trabalho em todo o mundo
observador.description: Georgieva afirma que, devido à IA, existem trabalhos que vão desaparecer e outros que serão redefinidos, sendo necessária a criação rápida de uma proteção para o "incrível poder" da IA.

observador.title: Videojogos. PJ sinaliza endereços usados para radicalização
observador.description: Operação decorreu no âmbito de uma ação coordenada pela Europol, com a participação de 16 países, que permitiu sinalizar "mais de nove mil ligações para conteúdos extremistas violentos e terroristas".

observador.title: Martin Matosa arbitra Benfica Lech Poznan
observador.description: Esloveno de 31 anos arbitrará pela primeira vez um jogo de uma equipa portuguesa. Jogo entre Benfica e polacos do Lech Poznan realiza-se na quinta-feira às 20h00 no Estádio da Luz.

france24fr.title: Midterms - Le démocrate James Talarico tente de convaincre le Texas, bastion républicain
france24fr.description: Au Texas, le dernier sénateur démocrate a été élu il y a 38 ans. Mais James Talarico essaye de changer la donne dans ce bastion républicain. Face à Ken Paxton, le démocrate tenait lundi 2 novembre au soir son dernier meeting avant les midterms, et ils étaient nombreux à venir le soutenir.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Israël : les coulisses de la couverture des élections
france24fr.description: Les résultats des législatives en Israël, qui ont notamment vu la percée de deux partis arabes, ne seront pas remis en cause par les soupçons d'irrégularités, a affirmé dimanche 1er novembre le président de la commission électorale. Les journalistes de France 24 se sont justement rendus sur place pour couvrir ces législatives mouvementées et encore dans l'incertitude du futur gouvernement. Les explications de Clovis Casali, journaliste et grand reporter à France 24.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle en France : y aura-t-il une primaire de la droite ?
france24fr.description: En France, le candidat Renaissance à la présidentielle Gabriel Attal, distancé dans les sondages par Édouard Philippe dans l'espace du centre et de la droite, a estimé lundi 2 novembre qu'une primaire de ce camp serait "inéluctable", malgré le refus du maire du Havre de se plier à l'exercice. Les précisions de Flore Simon, chroniqueuse politique à France 24.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : l'Afrique place trois nageuses dans le top six du 200 mètres brasse
france24fr.description: La nage mise à l'honneur lors des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse(JOJ) ce lundi 2 novembre à Dakar. La nageuse sud-afrcaine Chanel Veldsman a notamment remporté le bronze du 200 m brasse. Les précisions d'Elimane Ndao, correspondant France 24 au Sénégal.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : qui sont les lauréats de la bourse Ghislaine Dupont et Claude Verlon ?
france24fr.description: La bourse Ghislaine Dupont et Claude Verlon est décernée chaque année par RFI depuis 2014, en hommage à nos confrères assassinés dans le nord du Mali le 2 novembre 2013. Les deux lauréats de la 13e édition ont été annoncés ce soir à Madagascar : il s’agit de la journaliste Nadia Mam’tine Razaf et du technicien Yves Ramar'Sandjatana.

france24fr.title: Somalie : l'Ouganda commence le retrait de ses troupes après 20 ans de présence
france24fr.description: L'Ouganda a annoncé lundi 2 novembre avoir commencé le retrait de ses troupes déployées en Somalie. L'armée ougandaise est présente depuis 20 ans en Somalie dans le cadre d'un accord bilatéral, mais aussi via la Mission de soutien et de stabilisation de l'Union africaine en Somalie (Aussom), dont elle est une composante majeure.  Les précisions d'Aurore Bayoud, correspondante France 24 à Kigali.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : l'incarcération de l'opposant Prince Epenge ravive les tensions
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l'opposant Prince Epenge arrêté la semaine dernière, en fin octobre, est en prison à Makala. L'arrestation puis la détention de cette figure de l'opposition cristallise les tentions avec la majorité au pouvoir. Le président Félix Tshisekedi a affirmé vouloir engager un dialogue national pour résoudre la crise. Les précisions d'Emmet Livingstone, correspondant France 24 à Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: Trump annonce mettre fin à une aide annuelle de 3,8 milliards de dollars à la sécurité d'Israël
france24fr.description: Le président des États-Unis a annoncé mardi une coupe de 3,8 milliards de dollars dans l'assistance annuelle à la sécurité d'Israël. Il a assuré que cette décision avait été prise en accord avec le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu.

france24fr.title: Goncourt 2026 : "le prix changera ma carrière, mais certainement pas ma vie"
france24fr.description: Philippe Jaenada a obtenu mardi 3 novembre le prestigieux prix Goncourt 2026 pour "L'Inconnue du quai de Javel", roman sur l'assassinat irrésolu d'une jeune Bretonne en 1949, au terme d'une sélection percutée par l'affaire Thélyson Orélien. Après avoir exprimé sa joie, l'écrivain de 62 ans a confié que "le prix changera ma carrière, mais pas ma vie, certainement pas". Les précisions de Noémie Roche, journaliste France 24, en direct du restaurant Drouant, où s'est déroulé la remise.

france24fr.title: Mobilisations en France : nouveaux blocages de facs et de lycées
france24fr.description: En France, les lycéens et les étudiants comptent bien ne "rien lâcher", jugeant les mesures annoncées par le gouvernement insuffisantes. Le ministère de l'Éducation nationale a annoncé le blocage de 48 lycées et 51 établissements de l'enseignement supérieur sur 184 sont perturbés. Un des étudiants du Campus de Jussieu affirme qu'il est d'ailleurs "de plus en plus compliqué d'aller manifester". Les explications de Johan Bodin, journaliste France 24 en direct du Campus de Jussieu à Paris.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : des frappes russes massives font des dégâts sur le réseau énergétique
france24fr.description:
Le ⁠président Volodimir Zelensky, qui ​est attendu ce mardi 3 novembre à Berlin, a ​déclaré que l'Ukraine avait été la cible de nouvelles attaques russes dans la nuit, notamment de 289 drones, ​contre ‌ses infrastructures énergétiques. Le président ukrainien a ⁠également fait état des tirs de 17 missiles balistiques et de ‌59 missiles de croisière de la part

de ⁠l'armée russe.

france24fr.title: Midterms : un référendum pour taxer les milliardaires en Californie
france24fr.description: Lors des midterms débutée ce mardi 3 novembre, des questions locales sont aussi abordés. En Californie, un référendum d'origine populaire sera particulièrement scruté : celui d'une taxe sur les milliardaires. L'idée serait de prélever 5 % en une fois de la fortune des 250 milliardaires de Californie. Une mesure qui rapporterait 100 milliards de dollars. Les précisions de Loïc Pialat, correspondant France 24 à Los Angeles.

france24fr.title: Midterms : le président pourrait-il poser son veto en cas de victoire des démocrates ?
france24fr.description: Les midterms engagées ce mardi 3 novembre aux États-Unis permettra de décider de la suite du mandat de Trump. Si ces élections sont remportées par le Parti démocrate, un tiers des sénateurs, un tiers des gouverneurs et tous les postes au niveau de congrès des cinquante États pourrait être remplacés, bien que le président Trump apparaît tenté de s'opposer à ces changements. Les précisions d'Anne Deysine, professeure émérite de l'université Paris-Nanterre.

france24fr.title: Midterms : l'augmentation du prix de l'essence est au cœur du scrutin dans le Maine
france24fr.description: Le prix de l'essence en constante inflation depuis la guerre en Iran est au cœur des préoccupations de très nombreux États-uniens, notamment les électeurs du Maine qui s'apprêtent à élire un sénateur lors des midterms débutées ce mardi 3 novembre.

france24fr.title: Midterms : ouverture des bureaux de vote sur la côte est, le compte à rebours est lancé
france24fr.description: Les États-uniens votent mardi 3 novembre lors d'élections cruciales à valeur de référendum sur Donald Trump, l'opposition démocrate espérant remporter une double majorité au Congrès. Les bureaux de vote ont ouvert à 06 h 00 heure locale dans de nombreux États de la côte est. Des élections aux enjeux importants et pour lesquelles près de 58 millions de citoyens ont déjà voté par anticipation, un record pour des "midterms". Les précisions de Matthieu Mabien, correspondant France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: La Pologne affirme avoir déjoué une possible provocation à la frontière russe avec Kaliningrad
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre polonais, Donald Tusk, a déclaré, mardi, qu'une possible provocation avait été déjouée dans la nuit à la frontière avec l'enclave russe de Kaliningrad. Les services polonais n'ont pour le moment pas confirmé s'il s'agissait d'une tentative d'agression russe.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Sénégal : l'Assemblée nationale, contrôlée par l'opposition, rejette le projet de budget rectificatif 2026
Au Sénégal, un budget crucial rejeté par l'Assemblée nationale
france24fr.description: La crise politique autour du projet de loi de finances s'aggrave au Sénégal. L'Assemblée nationale a rejeté mardi le budget révisé présenté par le gouvernement. Le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye subit ainsi un revers de la part de son ancien allié Ousmane Sonko, leader du principal parti d'opposition, le Pastef.

spiegel.title: Cottbus: Schüler getreten und geschlagen – Lehrer erhält Bewährungsstrafe
spiegel.description: Er hatte ein Kind so schwer verletzt, dass es ins Krankenhaus kam: Ein Lehrer ist in Cottbus zu einem Jahr und einem Monat Freiheitsstrafe auf Bewährung verurteilt worden. Der Mann legte ein Geständnis ab.

spiegel.title: »Gen Z regelt«-Proteste: Am 20. November soll wieder protestiert werden - nur wer hat das Sagen?
spiegel.description: Zehntausende gingen bei den »Gen Z regelt«-Protesten auf die Straße. Doch nun sind die Organisatoren uneins, wie es weitergehen soll – und wer das Sagen hat.

spiegel.title: Cyberkriminalität: Angriff zwingt CAP-Supermarkt in Wuppertal zur Entsorgung von Ware
spiegel.description: Hacker sabotieren das Kühllager, der Wuppertaler CAP-Supermarkt muss Ware für 25.000 Euro wegwerfen. Hier erzählt Geschäftsführer Christoph Nieder, wie er sich seitdem schützt – und ob er den Schaden ersetzt bekommt.

spiegel.title: Arabische Wähler in Israel: Schawarma ja, Koalition nein
spiegel.description: Ohne die arabischen Parteien lässt sich in Israel kaum eine Regierung bilden – doch die jüdischen Politiker wollen keine Zusammenarbeit. In den arabischen Städten fragen sich die Menschen: Was für eine Demokratie soll das sein?

spiegel.title: Leag: Doppelte Staatsgelder für Kohlekraftwerke
spiegel.description: Der Lausitzer Stromerzeuger bekommt 1,75 Milliarden Euro, weil er alte Kohlekraftwerke vorzeitig abschaltet. Und nochmals Staatsgeld, um die Meiler zu Gaskraftwerken umzubauen. Das kann rechtlich nicht sauber sein.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Midterms in den USA, Selenskyj in Berlin, Halloween-Horror
spiegel.description: In den USA wackelt Trumps Mehrheit im Kongress. Der Kanzler ringt um Einfluss in der Ukrainediplomatie. Und: Wer steckt hinter den gefährlichen Halloween-Süßigkeiten? Das ist die Lage am Dienstagabend.

spiegel.title: Renten sollen im kommenden Jahr um mehr als vier Prozent steigen
spiegel.description: Die Bundesregierung erwartet 2027 eine Rentenerhöhung von mehr als vier Prozent. Der Beitragssatz bleibt stabil, soll aber in den kommenden Jahren steigen.

spiegel.title: Schimpfwörter-Ausstellung in Hof: Museum sammelt Flüche aus der Region
spiegel.description: Was haben Klöße mit Köpfen zu tun? Wie motzt man über Männer? Und warum denken wir beim Poltern gern an Fäkalien? Ein Museum in Bayern hat nach Schimpfwörtern gesucht. Die Direktorin sagt: Fluchen ist gesund.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: USA wollen Israel künftig keine Militärhilfen mehr zahlen
spiegel.description: Die USA stellen offenbar die finanzielle Unterstützung für Israels Militär ein – mindestens zwei Jahre früher als geplant. Der Zeitpunkt ist wohl bewusst gewählt.

spiegel.title: Vanessa Emde: Linke in Berlin vertagt erneut Entscheidung im Fall der umstrittenen Abgeordneten
spiegel.description: Die Neuköllner Abgeordnete Vanessa Emde ist zur Belastung für die rot-grün-rote Koalitionsbildung in Berlin geworden. Sie provozierte auch ihre Parteifreunde. Doch Konsequenzen hat das bislang kaum.

spiegel.title: Palm Beach: Flugzeug-Absturz in Florida – Wie eine Rakete, die mitten im Wohngebiet einschlägt

phys-org.title: An asteroid's shape influences where a nuclear blast must be aimed to deflect it
phys-org.description: If a dangerous asteroid were headed toward Earth, one defense could be a nuclear detonation to blast one side with X-rays and nudge it off course. But new simulations suggest that for a lumpy, irregular asteroid, exactly where those X-rays hit could make a huge difference.

phys-org.title: New survey measures make double consciousness testable in studies of Black Americans
phys-org.description: W.E.B. Du Bois' standing as a distinguished social scientist, with a distinguished body of work, has been subjected to the same marginalizing forces he examined in his pioneering scholarship on race, culture and Black social thought.

phys-org.title: A type of Arctic Ocean bacteria may be using acetone to turn carbon into food
phys-org.description: A newly identified Arctic Ocean bacterium may have an unusual way of making the building blocks it needs to grow. Using acetone, a common chemical in seawater, the bacteria incorporate carbon dioxide (CO₂) into their metabolisms, allowing them to survive in waters where nutrients and usable organic matter are scarce.

phys-org.title: Research ties heat to mealybug feeding and pasture damage
phys-org.description: High temperatures change how mealybugs feed, and that could help explain why some pasture mealybug infestations do far more damage than others, according to early findings from Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists.

phys-org.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
phys-org.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning more than 40 years and brings physicists closer to exploring the "Zeptoverse"—an unexplored world that exists at distances of a billionth of a trillionth of a meter, or a "zeptometer," where new particles and forces of nature may be hiding

phys-org.title: How to reduce harmful sexual behavior and protect your kids and their peers
phys-org.description: Recent media reports of alleged sexual assaults by teenage boys draw attention to an uncomfortable truth: Young people sometimes perpetrate harmful sexual behavior against their peers.

phys-org.title: Afforestation reshapes wildfire activity across temperate regions worldwide
phys-org.description: Tree planting provides wood, biomass and climate benefits, but the location where those new forests are established matters. An international study by researchers in Spain, Chile and Finland shows that converting nonforested land into planted forests can increase wildfire activity, with contrasting outcomes across temperate regions.

phys-org.title: Forgotten flint tools reveal how Egypt's farmers organized work before the pharaohs
phys-org.description: More than a century after they were excavated from beneath Cairo, almost 3,000 stone tools from Heliopolis show that specialized work was already reshaping village life before Egypt became a state.

phys-org.title: JWST may have found where heavy black hole seeds formed
phys-org.description: Astrophysicists think that the supermassive black holes (SMBH) we see in the modern universe are the result of a long, drawn-out process. That process is referred to as the hierarchical black hole mergers framework. It explains how some SMBHs can reach such staggering masses. Some of the most massive appear to have billions of solar masses.

phys-org.title: 'Evolution in the act': Forest lizards reveal rapid adaptation in a warming world
phys-org.description: Yale research scientist Saúl Domínguez-Guerrero didn't set out to catch "evolution in the act" when he traveled to the Caribbean with a team of Yale researchers a few years ago. At the time, the team from the lab of evolutionary biologist Martha Muñoz planned to do fieldwork on Caribbean anoles, colorful, tree-dwelling lizards native to warmer regions of the Americas.

phys-org.title: Many local communities know how to communicate during disasters. Let's learn from them
Beetle poop may have helped shape millions of years of yeast evolution
phys-org.description: University at Buffalo scientists have found evidence that different species of yeast have shared genes originally acquired from an ancient virus—and the guts and droppings of beetles may have helped make it happen.

phys-org.title: Why we give flowers to those in grief—or buy them for ourselves when we're sad
phys-org.description: During his renowned excavations at the Shanidar Cave in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, American archaeologist Ralph Solecki located burial sites containing pollen and flower fragments from various species of wildflowers. He interpreted this as evidence that Neanderthals may have placed flowers around their dead at their burial sites around 60,000 years ago.

phys-org.title: Why are we so squeamish about eating hagfish?
phys-org.description: When fishers are out working their boats, they are typically targeting a specific type of fish. However, other species often end up in their nets or trawls as well. This is known as "bycatch"—seafood for which the fishers receive no payment. Although it is illegal to discard bycatch back into the sea, it still happens.

phys-org.title: Fingernail-sized chip untangles mixed light into clean beams
phys-org.description: Stanford engineers and colleagues designed a chip that can take a muddled mixture of light from multiple lasers and output clean beams of light. It's the first time researchers have demonstrated a device that can take in mixed, or partially coherent, light and sort its photons into a clear set of separate beams.

phys-org.title: Trial of live facial recognition technology to catch criminals is putting people's privacy to the test
phys-org.description: WA Police are using live facial recognition technology to help identify and arrest criminals, with significant results. The trial is the first of its kind in Australia.

phys-org.title: A tiny shift exposes a cold brown dwarf masquerading as an early galaxy
phys-org.description: A faint red object spotted by the James Webb Space Telescope originally appeared to offer a possible glimpse of the universe's first galaxies. But images taken about 3½ years apart revealed a giveaway: The object, nicknamed Capotauro, had moved.

phys-org.title: Unpacking wheat's water use for drought research
phys-org.description: Researchers at The University of Queensland have developed a way to quantify how wheat varieties capture and convert soil water. Dr. Raul Gimenez from the Queensland Alliance for Agriculture and Food Innovation said the technique could be used to identify drought-tolerant crops.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Tariff Fiasco Could Save Free Trade
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have raised prices and hurt businesses without reducing the trade deficit or creating manufacturing jobs. But global trade has held up better than expected, and growing public opposition to tariffs could pave the way for a retreat from protectionism.

proj-syn.title: If AI Thinks for Us, Democracy Will Suffer
proj-syn.description: Whereas the internet buried us in information, AI enables us to outsource analysis altogether. But when it comes to grappling with humanity’s most important questions, we must resist the temptation and recognize that we all have a duty—to each other and to ourselves—to keep “showing up.”

proj-syn.title: A Tory Mentor for the MAGA GOP
proj-syn.description: Kemi Badenoch’s keynote address at the British Conservative Party conference last month outlined her plan for a pro-growth future that respects fiscal discipline and human dignity. As American conservatives look beyond Donald Trump and to the 2028 primary campaign, they should embrace a similar agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Politics of Poland’s Judicial Crisis
proj-syn.description: The removal of Bogdan Święczkowski as president of the Constitutional Tribunal has triggered a physical confrontation at the court and a political standoff between Donald Tusk’s government and the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party. But Święczkowski was not so much removed as barred, because he held the position illegally.

proj-syn.title: Mapping AI Resistance
proj-syn.description: Since a society that is reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains, it is worth understanding why the AI revolution is being welcomed in some places and resisted in others. The explanation is not as simple as headline poll data and much media coverage suggest.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Perilous Ebola Complacency
proj-syn.description: The exponential trajectory of the latest Ebola outbreak is an urgent reminder that infectious diseases do not wait for ideal geopolitical alignments or balanced budgets. Global leaders must fund the Africa-led regional response today, or risk paying an immeasurably higher price in human lives and economic devastation tomorrow.

proj-syn.title: Industrial Decarbonization Is Good for Business
proj-syn.description: With major governments showing open hostility toward climate solutions or focusing on other needs, one might think that progress toward decarbonization is in jeopardy. Yet across the global industrial sector, many companies are increasing productivity, boosting revenue growth, and reducing emissions all at once.

proj-syn.title: When the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Speculative bubbles often leave behind valuable infrastructure while bankrupting the investors who financed them. AI could follow the same path, but the industry’s growing reliance on borrowed money raises the risk of a major financial crisis long before its world-beating applications emerge.

proj-syn.title: After Brazil and Serbia’s Elections
proj-syn.description: The recent electoral defeat of far-right forces in Brazil and Serbia offers important lessons for pro-democracy forces around the world as they confront nationalist and illiberal movements. But no single election can guarantee democracy’s resilience, and the challenges these countries’ new governments face remain formidable.

proj-syn.title: The New Geopolitics of Mining
proj-syn.description: While the US and China want their critical-mineral investments to deliver the biggest returns possible, governments in resource-rich countries must balance external pressures with internal demands. Mining firms must also win local communities’ trust, as host countries will be quick to throw them under the bus if public opinion sours.

proj-syn.title: Can Bond Vigilantes Prevent the Next Debt Crisis?
proj-syn.description: With interest rates on government debt having gone from near zero to much higher levels in recent years, rising short- and long-term bond yields have cast doubt on the sustainability of some debts and led many to wonder if a crisis might be looming. While some countries are more protected than others, none is immune.

proj-syn.title: A Wealth Tax Would Harm California
proj-syn.description: Before approving a one-time tax on the wealth of billionaires who lived in the state at a certain point in time, Californians should consider what such a policy will do to future tax revenues. Since wealth is mobile, those who stand to lose the most will simply leave, taking their future income-tax payments with them.

proj-syn.title: A Future for Europe’s Youth
proj-syn.description: The current generation of young Europeans possesses freedoms, material resources, opportunities to travel, and technological capabilities beyond anything previous generations could have imagined. Their demands, however, are strikingly simple: decent schools, secure jobs, affordable homes, and the possibility of raising a family.

proj-syn.title: A Tale of Two Chinas
proj-syn.description: China’s economy is deeply unbalanced, with a battered real-estate sector, weak consumption, and stark regional disparities coexisting with dynamic tech and export sectors. But provided that political stability is maintained, China could continue to be a global powerhouse even as hundreds of millions of its citizens remain poor.
